newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on weather and soy decline.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on weather and soy decline.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on nearly ideal weather in the U.S. Midwest and on a drop in soybeans, traders said.
"Weather improved and that's why we were down," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
The U.S. corn crop was seeded at a near-record pace and recent wet weather and warmer temperatures led to prospects for excellent crop yields.
Traders also said a drop in wheat futures lent pressure to the corn futures market and export news, while supportive, failed to ward off the pressure from other fronts.
USDA early Monday said U.S. corn export inspections during the week ended June 12 totaled 29.308 million bushels, above expectations for 21 million to 24 million bushels.
Fund selling totaled at least 11.0 million bushels and commercial selling also was noted. Cargill Inc sold eight million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn closed two to 5-3/4 cents lower, with July down three cents at $2.68-1/2 per bushel and December down 5-3/4 at $2.48-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 45,000 contracts, above the 43,815 traded Friday.
In corn options, Lind Waldock bought 1,500 December $2.50 puts at 12 to 13 cents, Smith Barney sold 750 December $2.60 calls at 9-1/2 cents and sold 500 July $2.60 calls at 9-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, above the 13,953 traded Friday.
